request.spec:
A claim may carry tags: a comma separated text on the claim form, each tag trimmed and lower-cased,
repeats dropped; the claim shows its tags sorted, comma and space separated. The form can change a
claim's tags when it can edit the claim. For every tag ever used on the sheet, the sheet shows a
due-total per tag: the due of the claims that count which carry it (a claim with two tags counts in
both). CLAIM_ADDED gains tags=<comma separated, sorted> at its end when any were given. A claim
split off another carries the original's tags.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
A claim may carry tags: a comma separated text on the claim form, each tag trimmed and lower-cased,
repeats dropped; the claim shows its tags sorted, comma and space separated. The form can change a
claim's tags when it can edit the claim. For every tag ever used on the sheet, the sheet shows a
due-total per tag: the due of the claims that count which carry it (a claim with two tags counts in
both). CLAIM_ADDED gains tags=<comma separated, sorted> at its end when any were given. A claim
split off another carries the original's tags.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit

you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
Claims can now carry tags, and all 4 tests in `bin/e2e` pass.

**Stored data**
- A new migration, `V56__claim_tags.sql`, adds a `tags` column on `claim`. Tags are stored trimmed, lower-cased, without repeats, sorted and comma-joined (e.g. `a,b`), or null when there are none.
- It also adds a `sheet_tag` table that keeps every tag ever used on a sheet. That way a tag still gets its due-total after no claim carries it any more, for example when a draft is edited to drop it.

**Server**
- A new helper, `Tags.java`, does the cleaning up of the typed text.
- The claim form accepts `tags`. Adding a claim and editing one both save them. Editing only the amount keeps the tags the claim already has.
- `CLAIM_ADDED` gets ` tags=a,b` at the end of the line, only when tags were given.
- A claim split off another copies the original's tags.
- The claim shows its tags as `a, b`, or empty when it has none. When the sheet is viewed as of a date, the tags shown are the claim's current ones, the same way the note and reference work.
- There is a new `GET /api/sheets/{id}/tags` endpoint that lists every tag ever used on the sheet. It ignores the as-of date, so it always gives today's list.

**Front end**
- The claim form has a `claim-form-tags` field and each claim row has a `claim-tags` cell.
- The people list shows one `tag-<tag>-due-total` per tag, under the sheet totals. It adds up the due of the claims that count (the same rule the person totals use), so a claim with two tags counts in both. Unlike the sheet's due-total, these sums don't drop the highest and lowest person and aren't capped.

Two limits:
- Paste and quick-add can't set tags; only the claim form can.
- Text over 1,000 characters in the tags field is rejected with the general "could not be added/saved" message, not one specific to tags.
